title: Romania's  Central Bank  cuts rates, leu may suffer.
text:
BUCHAREST, Jan 3 (Reuter) - Romania's Central Bank cut its key interest rates on Tuesday, stirring fears that the leu currency may depreciate in reaction to the cuts unless the Central Bank intervenes. 

 The National Bank of Romania (BNR) cut its reference rate to an annual 55 percent from 58 percent and its overdraft rate to 105 percent a year from 130 percent, a bank official said. 

 The reference rate is the central bank indicative rate while its overdraft rate is the rate it charges when banks borrow from their account at BNR. 

 "The cuts were in line with decreasing inflation and expectations of low inflation in the next months," Cezar Botel deputy manager of the central bank said. 

 Dealers were less sanguine. "Without central bank intervention I see the leu down at around 1,800 to the dollar," one dealer said. 

 On Tuesday the leu opened around 1,775/85 to the dollar, down from its 1,770/85 level on Friday's close. 

 BNR governor Mugur Isarescu last week said the bank was ready to step into the market if necessary as it did in December, when it spent $20-30 million to support the leu. 

 Traders said there was a shortage of dollars on the market and they believed it was not only a seasonal phenomenon. 

 "The dollar became attractive lately as gains from interest on lei deposits fell over the past few months. People have to protect their lei and so far they don't have other alternatives which could offer higher earnings," a dealer said. 

 Dealers generally declined to commit themselves to any long-term forecasts saying they were waiting for the reaction of the commercial banks to the interest rates cut. 

 Commercial banks' interest rates are currently at 65 percent a year and analysts said they expect banks to follow the central bank move to reduce rates. 

 BNR's Isarescu said he expected inflation in the year to end-December 1994 to fall to 66 percent from 295.5 percent in 1993 compared with a 75 percent forecast under an IMF restructuring programme.

title: FOCUS-Romania C.Bank confident, cabinet debates reforms.
text:
BUCHAREST, July 24 (Reuters) - Romania's central bank (BNR) on Friday said a lower discount rate and new rules on reserves reflected confidence in economic trends while the cabinet debated for the second straight day how to speed up reforms. 

 The BNR statement, issued two days after the changes were first leaked, said that a cut in the discount rate to 35 from 40 percent, valid August 1, showed its belief that inflation had been tamed. 

 It also gave a signal to relaunch lending activity after months of contraction in line with Romania's recession. 

 The statement said the new rules aimed to "direct money supply and interest rates in line with inflation. Meanwhile, a positive signal has been given to relaunch credit activity." 

 Monthly inflation fell to 1.3 percent in June from a peak of 7.2 percent in February. Officials put the average monthly inflation rate at between 1.7 to two percent by the year's end. 

 Inflation remains one of the few bright spots in Romania's economic outlook, with investors and Western lenders demanding faster action on long-delayed privatisation and restructuring of top-heavy industry left over from communist times. 

 At the government headquarters, Prime Minister Radu Vasile and his cabinet were debating for the second consecutive evening how to put utilities and other large enterprises more quickly into private hands. 

 Ministers were to approve the restructuring of Romgaz gas authority and a fund to protect farmers' incomes, which were threatened by wheat imports from more efficient neighbouring markets. 

 Vasile, appointed in April to end months of debilitating rows within the cabinet, blamed both his privatisation and finance ministers for slow progress with reforms and demanded measures to bring in more budget revenue. 

 The BNR circular notice sent to banks on Wednesday also announced that the Lombard rate of 140 percent would be replaced with a marginal rate of 95 percent starting August 1. 

 Under the new reserve requirements rules, the minimum reserve rate on leu currency rose to 15 from 12.5 percent, and the rate on hard currency funds fell to 15 from 20 percent. 

 The BNR also set a minimum daily reserve target ratio at 40 percent and a maximum ratio at 130 percent.

 The BNR has been keeping a tight grip on the markets in recent months, checking leu liquidity by soaking up deposits from banks or selling dollars to cushion the leu's slide. It has used both tolls in repeated interventions this week.

title: ROMANIA  CEN.BANK  INTERVENES  TO PROP UP EXPOSED LEU.
text:
BUCHAREST, Jan 30 (Reuters) - Romania's central bank (BNR) intervened on money and foreign currency markets on Friday to ease pressure on the leu amid rising dollar demand and an end to limits on individuals' foreign currency purchases. 

 The leu dipped about two percent on the interbank market, closing at 8,330/400 to the dollar, while retail prices remained relatively stable at 8,350/500. 

 The currency rebounded briefly after the BNR drained money market funds and sold modest amounts of dollars. 

 Most traders said the BNR's moves had failed to dissipate expectations of higher pressure on the unit. Leu liquidity is seen up and, while exchange offices were free of crowds, Romanians were still digesting the new regulations. 

 "Next week will be interesting," said one trader. "Much depends on what the BNR does. But higher bank deposit rates and maybe fresh government bonds issues for individuals could help offset the psychological impact of the rules." 

 Romania introduced new rules aligned to the International Monetary Fund's article eight on currency convertibility. These lifted the $500 annual limit on Romanians' hard currency purchases and allowed access to the interbank market. 

 The move had been carefully prepared for months by the BNR, which has pledged to take whatever action is needed to keep the leu from sliding too quickly. 

 With the new rules, Romania agrees not to impose curbs on payments and transfers for current account deals, essentially foreign trade, and not to operate multiple currency regimes. 

 But it can restrict capital movements. 

 BNR officials have repeateadly said the bank is prepared to keep a tight grip on the market. 

 Weeks of political turmoil, culminating in the walkout from the coalition cabinet on Thursday of its second largest party, the Social Democrats, have had little effect on the currency. But the party pledged to support the coalition in parliament. 

 Traders said no pressure had been detected from retail investors so far. Friday's slide, they said, could have been triggered by banks shifting to long dollar positions after staying short at the end of the month to meet minimum reserves. 

 Other operators said Romanians were likely to stick to a wait-and-see attitude as most banks increased deposit rates in response to rapid sales of high-interest government bonds. 

 "The bond sale was a clever move," said one dealer. "People were attracted by the new opportunities and if the Finance Ministry puts such papers on sale again the leu will gain." 

 Finance Minister Daniel Daianu said on Thursday before his departure for the World Economic Forum in Davos that he was confident the BNR "has full control of the situation. I'm not afraid of what might happen in the period ahead." 

 But he added that the leu's trend would depend on how solid an economic programme was put together by the revamped cabinet to emerge from this week's political upheaval. 

 Exchange house managers said no significant changes of their market features were likely ahead of the weekend. But some were reluctant to predict trends for next week. 

 "It's too soon to say what will happen. But in view of the BNR's efforts to create leu shortages it's possible there will be no spectacular shifts," said IDM exchange manager Dan Simionescu.

The PD national convention is expected to vote late Wednesday afternoon in a closed-door meeting. Party leadership has scheduled a press conference to comment on the vote for 18:00 local time (1600 GMT). 

Currency dealers said the controversy will also decide the immediate future of the leu, which the government says has suffered speculative attacks since the political crisis began last week. 

 One currency dealer with a foreign bank said the leu could face a confidence crisis under a weakened government coalition. The dealer said further pressure on the leu could force the government to delay plans to adopt, in February, Article VIII of the International Monetary Fund charter on internal currency convertibility. 

 To adopt the article, the government must scrap legislation forcing exporters to immediately use dollar income to buy lei. The government would also have to eliminate legislation allowing Romanians to buy no more than $500 in hard currency per year. 

 Since the beginning of last week, the leu has depreciated to between 8,400 and 8,450 per dollar currently from between 8,250 and 8,300 per dollar despite steady intervention by the National Bank of Romania. 


Dealers estimate Romania's central bank has sold more than $60 million
this week and about $30 million last week.

title: Romania Importer Association Says Importer Dlr Demand Low
text:
BUCHAREST (Dow Jones)--Romania's National Association of Importers and Exporters Monday blamed speculators for weakening the leu over the last week and denied importer dollar buying had a significant effect on the currency. 

 In a press release Monday, association President Mihai Ionescu said imports, traditionally high in January, are considerably lower this month than last January and importer dollar demand has had only moderate effect on the leu. 

 Ionescu, who couldn't be immediately reached for comment, said in the press release that 'certain players' sparked a speculative attack on the leu 'at the first sign of an increase' in the dollar rate. 

 The press release also blamed the National Bank of Romania for not intervening in currency markets last Thursday or Friday. 

 As reported, Romania's central bank sold about $10 million daily in the first three days of last week but refrained from intervention at the end of the week. 

 The statement comes after local media cited the National Bank of Romania blaming foreign bank speculation for weakening the leu last week. 

 As reported, the leu has depreciated to between 8,480 and 8,570 per dollar Monday afternoon from between 8,250 and 8,300 per dollar a week earlier. 

Currency dealers say increased dollar demand from importers,
particularly oil buyers, has weakened the leu.

title: FOCUS - ROMANIA C.BANK ACTS TO CUSHION LEU DOWNSWING.
text:
BUCHAREST, Dec 4 (Reuters) - Romania's central bank (BNR) intervened on the local interbank market on Thursday, selling dollars and draining money market funds to cushion a downswing of the leu currency, dealers said. 

 The BNR moves intensified a campaign in recent days to offset increased pressure on the currency. 

 "The leu is faced with larger hard currency purchases from imports and some repatriation of capital market gains," said one dealer. 

 "A rise in leu liquidity at the beginning of the month also hit the leu's relative stability," another dealer said. 

 Most players said market trends were unaffected by a vote in parliament to approve changes in Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's reshuffled cabinet aimed at rejuvenating reforms. 

 The leu recovered to near 7,920/970 to the dollar at midday from around 7,970/8,015 at Thursday's open, but remained weaker against last Friday's levels of 7,880/910. Short-term prices dipped to around 60/90 percent from 100/120 percent in early trading on Wednesday amid a cash-heavy money market. 

 Leu-dollar retail prices, generally more sensitive, remained relatively stable at 8,100/8,200. 

 The BNR acknowledged this week it had intervened on the foreign exchange markets in recent days, both selling and buying dollars to avoid undermining reserve money targets. 

 But officials said the bank was a net purchaser of hard currency last month, boosting its total foreign exchange reserves to 2.69 billion from end-October's 2.52 billion. 

 Dealers said the BNR seemed ready to continue to step into the market. "Maybe the BNR is willing to prepare us for the launch of the new currency rules and is trying to show it has guts to resist pressure," one trader said. h nearly doubled to 6.5 percent in October from the previous month. 

 Ciorbea said on Thursday the increase in the inflation rate was a temporary phenomenon and suggested it would stand somewhere below five percent in November. 

 Analysts said monthly inflation was likely to stay at about five percent in November and December as slow structural reforms were undermining this year's macro-stabilisation gains. 

 Traders said year-end bonuses and higher energy and transport prices were keeping inflationary expectations high, especially for December. 

 Romania's foreign exchange market was relatively calm in November, with hard currency purchases from clients at 440 million and sales at 436 million. The leu saw a gradual fall of about 1.4 percent after a similar slide in October.

title: Romania  c.bank confirms  interventions  on  fx  market.
text:
BUCHAREST, Dec 3 (Reuters) - Romania's central bank (BNR) has intervened on the local foreign exchange market, buying and selling hard currency to avoid undermining reserve money targets, BNR officials said on Wednesday. 

 "We have bought and sold dollars, seeking not only to avoid a sharper depreciation of the leu, but also to sterilise liquidity," BNR communication manager Adrian Vasilescu said. 

 "The BNR's move was aimed at draining leu funds from the market by selling dollars rather than taking deposits from the money market," Vasilescu said. 

 Reserve money, also known as the monetary base or high-powered money, includes cash in circulation and in vaults and banks' minimum reserves. 

 Dealers said the BNR sold dollars to contain a fast depreciation of the leu on Wednesday after the unit's ask quotes had fallen below 8,000 to the dollar amid growing hard currency demand. 

 They said the BNR sold dollars in several waves on Wednesday at prices ranging from 7,965 to 7,980, but Vasilescu declined to elaborate on prices or the size of interventions. 

 At midday, the leu recovered from its lows, helped by the BNR moves, and was trading at around 7,940/980 against opening levels of about 7,955/8,000 and nearer to its Tuesday's close. 

 Vasilescu said the BNR has also tried "to prevent further upward moves in interest rates." 

 The BNR has repeateadly mopped up leu deposits from the market in the past month, tightening its monetary policy to combat inflation. Its moves triggered a surge in short-term rates to more than 100 percent against 50 percent in late October. ((Mirela Eremia, Bucharest newsroom +40 1 312-0264))

title: ROMANIA CEN.BANK SAYS MONITORING TRADE BALANCE.
text:
BUCHAREST, Oct 6 (Reuter) - Romanian central bank governor Mugur Isarescu said on Monday the bank was closely watching trade balance figures to guard against movements in the leu currency affecting the country's competitiveness. 

 "We are not terribly worried. But revisions of trade figures have prompted new discussions on external (balance of payments) adjustments," Isarescu told a news conference. 

 "An appreciation in the currency in real terms in April and May affected the competitiveness of exports." 

 Isarescu said the leu's short-term moves would be monitored. Monetary and interest rate moves as well as market interventions would be used to keep leu investments attractive. 

Romania's trade deficit widened to $187.4 million in July from $174.2 million in June, as imports grew more quickly than exports. The January-July deficit was $856.2 million. 

 The leu plunged to nearly 9,000 to the dollar in March but recovered smartly to levels around 7,000 throughout the summer. It has slipped in recent weeks to 7,700, with the central bank periodically intervening to prevent sharp declines. 

 Iscarescu said that in the long run the BNR was considering a currency corridor to make the exchange rate more predictable. 

 "We are considering an increase in transparency and predictibility," Isarescu said. 

 He said any corridor or trading band would differ from a classic crawling-peg system. He suggested the model of the "diagonal band" used in Israel, under which the currency moves in accordance with inflation and the balance of payments. 

 "We need a market-determined exchange rate," he said. "Until annual inflation is cut well below 20 percent, I favour flexibility of the exchange rate though I realise the need of more predictibility."

 Isarescu said that in the long run the BNR was considering a currency corridor to make the exchange rate more predictable. 

 "We are considering an increase in transparency and predictability," Isarescu said. 

 He said any corridor or trading band would differ from a classic crawling-peg system. He suggested the model of the "diagonal band" used in Israel, under which the currency moves in accordance with inflation and the balance of payments. 

 "We need a market-determined exchange rate," he said. "Until annual inflation is cut well below 20 percent, I favour flexibility of the exchange rate though I realise the need of more predictability."

title: Romania's Leu Seen Facing Winter Test In  Currency  Markets
text:
BUCHAREST -(Dow Jones)- Winter purchases of oil, although lower than in 1996, may cause Romania's leu to depreciate more quickly over the coming months, traders said. 

 The leu's weakness may be compounded by the removal of regulations limiting individuals from purchasing more than $500 in foreign currency, although these pressures may be balanced by a long-expected - but yet to materialize - inflow of foreign investment to the country's securities markets. 

 The first hint of greater volatility in the foreign-exchange markets came last week, when the National Bank of Romania intervened to support the currency. Since the currency market was liberalized in March, the National Bank has allowed the leu to depreciate in line with inflation, while boosting its foreign-exchange reserves by buying dollars on an almost daily basis. 

 Some analysts doubt the National Bank will be prepared to use its currency reserves to support the leu if it does begin to fall more quickly. 

 Parvoleta Shtereva, an analyst with ING Barings in London, said the central bank acted rapidly to halt the leu's slide last week, but doubted whether it will do the same in the near future. 

 "I still don't believe they'll be prepared to do this on a daily basis," said Shtereva. "They certainly don't want to bleed reserves all through the fourth quarter." 

 Shtereva said that with reserves at about $2.5 billion the central bank has the means, if not the will, to stabilize the leu. 

 But she said the central bank will be reluctant to part with reserves that it has raised from $700 million in January. 

 Shtereva predicts the leu will reach 8,200 per dollar by the end of the year, while Paul Dinescu, treasury director of ABN Amro in Bucharest, believes the leu will end the year at about 8,000 per dollar. 

 The leu settled Monday at about 7,600 to the dollar, after the dollar rose to as high as 7,720 lei last Tuesday. 

 Traders say oil imports may be the most important factor in the foreign-exchange market until energy demand subsides early next year. They say state oil importer Petrol Export-Import has already bought $100 million in September, and will likely buy another $50 million in coming weeks before stepping up purchases again in November. 

 Oil imports are expected to be lower than the 3.2 million tons purchased in 1996, reflecting an expected 2% decline in gross domestic product from last year. 

 However, there may be additional pressure on the leu beginning in October, when the central bank enacts legislation to allow Romanian citizens to buy as much hard currency as they want. Romanians can currently buy a maximum of $500 per year but the central bank says it will change the legislation to adopt International Monetary Fund standards on internal currency convertibility. 

 Traders say private Romanians, with an average monthly wage of about $80, can't buy enough dollars to have a medium-term effect on the leu. But private foreign-exchange bureaus may want to stock up on foreign currency in advance of the new legislation, so there could be a short-term impact on the currency, say traders. 

 Romania's fledgling capital markets are the least predictable factor and could force the central bank to protect the leu from either steep depreciation or appreciation. 

 Romanian stock brokers have been predicting the arrival of a flood of foreign investment ever since the government began to remove restrictions on the repatriation of foreign investments in July. 

 Such a flood would boost the leu, and force the central bank to maintain the near-daily dollar purchases it has conducted over the last six months. 

 But if anything, foreign investment appears to be slowing down. During a stock market rally in June and early July, foreign investment pushed daily trading volumes up to more than 20 billion lei. But despite the listing of about 20 new shares since then, trading volume now averages about eight billion lei per day as domestic investors regain some market dominance and shares prices drop.

title: Romania  leu ends weaker despite c.bank  intervention .
text:
BUCHAREST, Sept 26 (Reuter) - Romania's leu ended lower at about 7,600/645 to the dollar on Friday against opening quotes of around 7,560/630 despite central bank (BNR) moves to sell dollars and temper a midday downswing, dealers said. 

 "The BNR sold dollars to all players who had bid quotes weaker than 7,600," said one trader. 

 The leu managed a slight recovery in afternoon trading after the BNR intervention, but eased back to weaker quotes at close, traders said. 

 Most said the leu's trend for next week depended on the BNR's further moves in the coming days, when pressure on the unit might emerge from an expected rise in leu liquidity and larger dollar buying orders from importers. 

 "Leu liquidity may rise with the start of a new month and following the cancellation of the treasury bill issue," said one trader, adding that the BNR might again mop up funds from the money market to keep the leu attractive. 

 Earlier in the day, the Finance Ministry said it cancelled a rollover issue worth 309.16 billion lei in six-month treasury bills due to cover papers maturing next week. It declined to say whether the other four issues of 91-day T-bills planned for next month would also be annulled. 

 Dealers said the BNR had refrained on Friday from draining leu funds as it had done in recent days to back the currency. Its previous moves on the money market imposed a rise in short-term prices, which traded now from 45 to 48 percent. 

 Other operators said the BNR might intervene again by selling hard currency on the interbank market if higher dollar demand pushed the leu sharply down. They said the BNR's aim was to avoid large fluctuations in the exchange rate. 

 BNR officials have pledged cautious policies to keep the unit competitive for exporters. 

 Local bankers said the BNR seemed to favour a gradual slide of the leu against the dollar, monitoring the market to prevent sharp moves and seeking to keep its reserves on target. Reserves are currently estimated at $2.3 billion. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264

title: ROMANIA  CEN BANK  INTERVENES  TO KEEP LEU LOW.
text:
BUCHAREST, May 28 (Reuter) - Operators on Romania's foreign exchange market said on Wednesday that the central bank had intervened to prevent the leu from appreciating after standing at 7,050/90 to the dollar for days. 

 "We are certain that the National Bank bank has intervened and bought large amounts of dollars," one dealer with a private bank said. 

 The leu closed the day weaker at 7,120/180 to the dollar. 

 "It is clear that their (BNR) action is meant to prevent the leu from firming." the dealer said. 

 BNR spokesman Mugur Stet denied any intervention by the bank saying Wednesday's dollar purchases had been in line with the central bank's policy to build up reserves. 

 "I admit we bought fairly large amounts of dollars over the past weeks," Stet told Reuters. "We had to buy because the market started being flooded with hard currency from portfolio investors to the capital market. So we had to take action," he said. 

 On Tuesday, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said the BNR's foreign exchange reserves stood at $1.6 billion, double the level recorded in February. 

 However, operators said on Wednesday the BNR had placed buying orders with a firm quotation by mid-day, departing from the "regular" pattern of late trading deals, usually with banks with long positions. 

 "There is no doubt that the central bank has bought a record amount of dollars from many banks today. It might be a signal to exporters," said another operator. 

 But dealers declined to elaborate on the range of BNR bids. 

 The daily Curierul National quoted BNR governor Mugur Isarescu as saying excess dollars on the market, amid a lower demand for credits, could prompt the central bank to intervene to drain the surplus and prevent the leu from firming. 

 Analysts warned a firmer leu could have a negative impact on reforms, affecting mainly exports and restructuring. 

 On Wednesday, dealers also said a T-bill issue worth 82 billion lei had not been sufficient to drain leu funds from the money market, in the absence of other banking instruments to mop up the excess.
